name: reply_stage_movement
description: Rep replies counted by the stage the deal moved to afterwards, with how long the move took. Use for 'do our replies move deals forward', 'how long after a reply does a deal progress', 'which replies lead somewhere'. READ THIS BEFORE DRAWING A CONCLUSION: a stage move after a reply is correlation, not proof the reply caused it. Deals move for many reasons and a rep reply is rarely the only thing happening. Say 'moved after' rather than 'worked' or 'caused'. stage_moved_to = 'None' means no stage change was recorded, which is the normal case for most replies, not a failure. under_15min_suspect counts moves recorded less than 15 minutes after the reply — too fast for a customer to have read and reacted, so almost certainly an automated CRM transition. On current data this is 2 of 791 replies (0.3%), so it is a rare artefact rather than a reason to distrust the view; report it only if it is non-trivial for the rows in question. buyer_type is the deal's PRIMARY type — a deal tagged with several is counted once, under the first.

params.name: stage_moved_to
params.description: Only replies followed by a move to this stage. 'None' for replies with no recorded move.

params.name: buyer_type
params.description: The deal's primary buyer type, lowercase.

params.name: min_replies
params.description: Only rows covering at least this many replies.

params.name: max_median_days
params.description: Only rows where the median move happened within this many days.
